en.text:
"...That deathly Ai-no-Yama song was being heard with a deathly heart. The five guests and the company gathered around them were not its only audience. One more person was listening."

"A half-story room projected beyond the courtyard. Room after room around it was bright; this one alone was strangely gloomy and dim. Naturally so. Here they kept women suffering from illness, women driven wild by their secret lovers,"

"and the room did two jobs: recovery and confinement. So its rumours were always in service. A woman had coughed blood and died here; a ghost appeared here. Such stories never stopped coming."

"Before the song began, a woman in that room had ground her ink and begun a letter. Already she had used a considerable length of the paper scroll."

"Furuichi's courtesans did not make a spectacle of Katsuyama hair and elaborate outer robes. They dressed plainly, like women outside the profession. On some, that simplicity sat very well indeed,"

"and stories of younger men staking their lives on love for an older woman in a white waist-wrap were not uncommon."

"The woman writing now was ill also. Even in that condition, she looked so thoroughly unlike a courtesan, so well did the plain appearance show her character."

en.text:
"Under the square vermilion lantern, her brush ran, stopped, ran again. Sometimes she wept. Then came that earlier verse—"

"The bells at dusk and dawn
Cry that extinction is bliss,
Yet none who hear are startled."

"She dropped the brush mid-letter and listened without moving. Otama's accompaniment flowed past in interwoven patterns."

"Though flowers scatter, spring will bloom.
Though birds return to their old nests,
The journey into death has no return."

Kanae"Aaah."
Sayo"And the injury to your leg, madam?"
Kanae"I cannot move it for now, but it is fine. Bones and tendons are not damaged."
Sayo"That is a relief... With your permission."
Kanae"...Nanny? The dressing can wait till later."
Kanae"It is not finished yet, anyway."
Sayo"No. We appear to have reached the final curtain. The cavalry has been taking its time very thoroughly, but at last it has favoured us with an appearance."
Kanae"Oh, such a pity. Saari mehnat hum karein, and they take the best part?"
Sayo"That, too, is the romantic heroine's allotted part. Ours, for now, is to withdraw."
Sayo"There may yet be an extra round. Regrettably, if we are caught up in it in our present condition, we will only be a hindrance."
Kanae"That would be very heroine-like too, in its way. Yes, you are right. Let us leave the rest to the knight, shall we?"
Sayo"Ji. To the knight..."
Kanae"..."
Sayo"..."
Kanae"You heard it, no?"
Sayo"At that distance, fragments only. The essential points, however, arrived quite clearly."
Sayo"Slipping a terminal into place, in case something like this should happen, was the correct decision. Sorimachi must be thanked."
Kanae"Yes. Thanks to it, a good deal has become visible..."
Kanae"Why he ended up dead. Is it not so, Nanny?"
Sayo"...Ji."

en.html:
Then she looked up.
The next shot would kill her. That was the enemy she faced.

The muzzle settled its aim. All the frustration this insignificant little opponent had caused it—now it meant to pour out the whole lot.

So, this far only.
Ichijou thought it.

No regret. Frustration, yes. More fighting, she had wanted that.

Beside him.
But once, at least, that wish had come true.

A long life spent tormenting herself because she could achieve nothing? Compared with that, this short fight and its ending had to be happiness. Surely.
That was what Ichijou Ayane thought.

Death accepted—she clenched her fist.

Until the end, fight.

そして見上げる。
　次こそは己を殺すであろう敵を。

　まさしく――
　物の数ならぬ小敵に溜め込まされた憤懣を、すべて
ぶち撒ける意思に満ちて、砲口が狙点を定める。

　ここまでか。
　一条は思った。

　悔いはない。
　悔しさはある――願わくばもっと戦いたかった。

　<ruby>あの人<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>と共に。
　しかしその願いは、一度だけだが叶えられたのだ。

　何も為し得ない己に悶々として長い生涯を過ごすの
に比べ、短い闘争の末に果てるこの今は、間違いなく
幸福に違いないと。
　綾弥一条はそう思った。

　死を受容し――
　そして彼女は拳を握る。

　最後まで戦うために。

en.html:
Her sense of direction was missing from birth. Such natural talent cannot be taught.

Good and evil, she could distinguish without blinking. Left and right were conducting a much more sophisticated deception. Justice had shown her the path. Very good. Now somebody please turn the girl around so she could walk on it.

Seedha jao. Go straight. She could do straight. The difficulty was which straight. The world, with its usual lack of consideration, had supplied more than one.
